obligation: G116 -- rANS net verdict: TOKEN_NS with consume-direct vs dense q3
the_A_B_WAS_NOT_RUN: The verify requires a paired A/B on the protected lane, and that needs the G115 kernel, which does not exist. No A/B is claimed.
what_IS_delivered_an_independent_check_o: G115 priced rANS decode at 1.83x q4 from its ALGORITHM. The roofline sweep already on disk tests that from a completely different direction -- measured machine ceilings rather than op counts -- and lands on the same number.
and_the_roofline_is_OPTIMISTIC_for_rANS: Worth keeping despite setting the magnitude aside: the sweep's own method note says it performs K FMAs on TWO INDEPENDENT CHAINS, so it measures THROUGHPUT rather than dependency latency. rANS decode is a SERIAL chain -- each state update feeds the next -- and cannot reach a ceiling measured on independent work. Whatever the roofline says about rANS is a lower bound on its cost.
the_verdict: PREDICTED LOSS, on the algorithmic route alone. rANS-q3 saves 40% of bytes against q4 and is priced at 1.83x the GEMV ALU on a machine measured ALU-issue bound and measured non-responsive to byte traffic. The roofline agrees in sign but its magnitude is not usable because it fails to reproduce the measured q4 GEMV. G116's acceptance says a LOSS is a valid closure and must be recorded as such -- but it also requires a paired A/B on the protected lane, which needs the G115 kernel. This is a twice-signed PREDICTION, not the closure.
what_would_change_it: Only a measured kernel. If the renormalisation predicates cleanly and the 7-symbol search folds into selects, the op count falls toward 6-7 and the ratio approaches parity. The roofline says even then rANS sits at 34.7 flop/byte where the sweep shows bandwidth already collapsing from 598 to 275 GB/s, so the operating point is unfavourable independent of the op count.

THE_ROUTES_DO_NOT_AGREE_AND_THE_ROOFLINE.why_they_differ: The roofline places q4 as BANDWIDTH-bound (22.75 ms floor against a 17.12 ms flop floor) and rANS as FLOP-bound (31.39 against 13.57). Different binding resources, so the ratio of binding floors is not the ratio of op counts. Same sign, 33% apart.
THE_ROUTES_DO_NOT_AGREE_AND_THE_ROOFLINE.the_consistency_check_the_roofline_FAILS: The roofline predicts a q4 GEMV floor of 22.75 ms. The MEASURED q4 GEMV is 20.616 ms -- the measurement BEATS the model's own floor by 10%. Implied effective bandwidth is 660 GB/s against the sweep's 598.3 GB/s peak. A model that cannot reproduce a measurement I already have must not be used to predict one I do not, so the roofline placement is recorded and then SET ASIDE rather than leaned on.
THE_ROUTES_DO_NOT_AGREE_AND_THE_ROOFLINE.consequence: The primary estimate stays G115's algorithmic 1.83x, which rests on a per-op rate fitted to a real kernel. The roofline corroborates the SIGN of the verdict and nothing more.
